item.title: Football fan jailed for threats over Di Maria return to Argentina
item.description: An Argentine court jailed a football supporter for seven and a half years on Wednesday for threatening Angel Di Maria in 2024 in a bid to stop the World Cup winner returning to Argentina at the end of his career. A court in Rosario found Sergio Di Vanni, 45, guilty of ordering acts of intimidation against Di Maria’s family with the aim of dissuading the former Argentina international from returning from abroad to play for a rival club. Di Maria was playing for Benfica at the time, in March 2024, but was considering a return to his boyhood club Rosario Central, a move he eventually completed in 2025. Rosario Central and Newell’s Old Boys, Lionel Messi’s childhood club, are the two major teams in Rosario and fierce local rivals. The threats included gunshots fired near a gated community where Di Maria owns a property and the dumping of a pig’s head bearing a bullet wound outside an estate agency run by his sister, alongside a message threatening his daughter. A 25-year-old woman, Belen Gutierrez, identified by prosecutors as one of the perpetrators, was sentenced to three and a half years in prison in June after entering a plea agreement. A third suspect remains in pre-trial detention. Prosecutors alleged the two carried out the threats in exchange for four million pesos ($2,600). According to the prosecution, the intimidation campaign was linked to an internal power struggle among Newell’s ultras. Di Vanni’s sentence also covered separate offences related to his involvement in the supporters’ group. Following the threats, Di Maria initially abandoned plans to return to Argentina for the safety of his family. He ultimately reversed that decision and, now 38, has spent the past two seasons at Rosario Central, helping the club win the Argentine title at the end of 2025. item.title: US judge rejects Trump admin interference in California midterm vote
item.description: A federal judge on Wednesday rejected the US Department of Justice’s efforts to set aside the ballots of more than 20,000 California voters it said might not be citizens, slamming the move as brazen pre-election “interference.” The case sparked an uproar ahead of the November 3 midterms, in which President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is at risk of losing its control of Congress, and appears to represent another attempt to cast doubt on electoral results. Democratic Party leaders have sued the Trump administration over the request, accusing Republicans of aiming “threats and intimidation” at state and local officials before the vote. US District Judge David O. Carter agreed, refusing to order the seizure of the ballots and siding with the government of Democratic-led California. “Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch,” Carter wrote in his decision. “Constitutional rights and our democracy are at stake. The public interest favors their protection,” he added. Those registered on California’s voter roles “must not be deprived of a core right merely because of unfounded allegations stemming from a procedure rife with uncertainty and errors.” The federal government in recent months had accused California of having 190,000 illegal voters on its books. It recently revised the figure to 20,000 and filed an emergency lawsuit about 10 days ago — after early voting had begun — to stop the state from sending ballots to them. A similar controversy arose in neighboring Nevada, where the allegations fizzled. The Trump administration had initially identified 16,000 non-citizen voters there, but after verification procedures that number dropped to 185 — and then to zero. “The DOJ’s actions are indicative of a broad, ongoing pattern of attempted election interference by federal officials,” Carter wrote in his decision. For months, Trump — who has never acknowledged his own election defeat by Joe Biden in 2020 — has been claiming that there will be fraud in this year’s midterms. Studies repeatedly show that while rare cases of voter fraud exist, such incidents are miniscule and do not influence election results. item.title: Troops kill 44 terrorists, scores injured in separate offensive in Borno
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have neutralised 44 suspected members of Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorists during several offensive operations in some parts of Borno State. The encounter also left scores of terrorists injured, with destruction of their vehicles, motorcycles and Improvised Explosive Device (IED) materials. These were disclosed by the Acting Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni in a press statement on Thursday morning. He said: “Troops of OPHK has sustained its offensive against terrorist elements through coordinated intelligence-led operations across the theatre. “On 26 October 2026, troops conducted engagements against suspected terrorist elements at separate locations in Kukawa Local Government Area of Borno State, following intelligence reports and surveillance observations. “Battle Damage Assessment indicated that 28 terrorists were neutralised, while six others reportedly sustained injuries. “In further operations on 28 October 2026, the Maritime Component, Naval Base Lake Chad deployed in Baga, conducted offensive actions against terrorist targets within the Lake Chad area. “Preliminary assessments indicated that eight terrorists were neutralised, while 10 others reportedly sustained varying degrees of injuries. “Separately, an air interdiction mission successfully disrupted a suspected terrorist improvised explosive device (IED)-laying operation, neutralising eight operatives and destroying their vehicle, motorcycles and IED materials. “The operation prevented the terrorist team from proceeding with its planned activity. “These successes reflect the sustained pressure being exerted on terrorist networks through intelligence-led joint operations,” Goni explained. He noted that OPHK remains committed to degrading terrorist capabilities, restricting their freedom of action and protecting communities across the North East. The Theatre Command urged members of the public to continue providing credible information to security agencies in support of ongoing efforts to restore lasting peace and security across the theatre. item.title: Esther Christian: Orphaned at 4, bags scholarship as debate champion at 15
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has offered full scholarship up to university level to 15-year-old Esther Christian, the captain of the Abia debate team that emerged victorious at the 2026 International Schools Debate Championship in Doha, Qatar. Christian, who lost her father at the age of four, will enjoy the scholarship through the Alex Otti Foundation. Otti announced the gesture while hosting the victorious students at the Michael Okpara Auditorium, Umuahia, where he also awarded N1 million each to the five students who represented Abia State and Nigeria at the international competition. The governor further awarded N1 million to Onyinyechi Okonkwo of Ovom Girls Secondary School, winner of a recent national essay competition; N750,000 each to officials who accompanied the debate team; and N1.75 million to Abia Model Basic Junior Secondary School, Abayi Umuocham, Osisioma Ngwa, which produced the champions. Presenting trophies, medals and certificates to the students, Otti reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to transforming the state’s education sector through sustained investment, improved infrastructure and wider access to quality education. “This is in the DNA of Abia State. We celebrate people. When you do well, we celebrate you,” the governor said. He also approved the team’s request to participate in the 2027 edition of the competition, noting that although progress had been recorded in the education sector, more work remained to be done. Earlier, the Chairman of the Abia State Universal Basic Education Board (ASUBEB), Mrs Lydia Ezinne Onuoha, who led the team to Qatar, said the students did not merely participate in the competition but distinguished themselves among more than 84 teams. She said the team won four trophies and 12 medals after defeating representatives of six countries. According to her, the students clinched the Best International School Debate Team, Overall Best Team in the Junior Category, Best Debater and Best Leadership awards. They also ranked among the tournament’s top 10 speakers. Onuoha disclosed that during the five final rounds, contestants were given impromptu topics and just 15 minutes to prepare and present their arguments. The Coordinator of the President’s Schools Debate Championship, Elder Oritu Dare, said the victory had created an opportunity for Nigeria to participate in the next edition of the competition in Singapore. He also commended the governor for infrastructural development in the state. The Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Elder Goodluck Ubochi, said the achievements recorded in the education sector were only the beginning, expressing confidence that sustained investment would produce better results. Similarly, the Abia State Coordinator of the Universal Basic Education Commission, Mrs Unyime Umoette, said public schools were becoming more functional and urged public office holders to adopt schools in their communities and support their development.

item.title: Soaring duties, FX rates cripple Nigeria’s used-vehicle market
item.description: •As dealers lament sales slump By Glory Bassey Car dealers in Nigeria have lamented a sharp decline in vehicle sales, blaming soaring import duties, high exchange rate and rising cost of living as reasons why car ownership is increasingly becoming unaffordable for many Nigerians. A car dealer and importer, Mr Paul Uche, said the auto market segment has experienced a significant change in prices and customer patronage, with most vehicles now selling over five times higher than the prices three years ago. Uche said that a 2005 Toyota Corolla that previously sold for about N1.5 million now costs between N8 million and N8.5 million, depending on its condition and grade. Similarly, a Toyota Camry 2010 model that sold for between N2.2 million and N3 million now goes for N9 million to N10 million. He said the situation had worsened this year, with sales dropping considerably compared with previous years, adding: “you can even stay three to four months without making any sales; the situation is frustrating for people struggling to keep their businesses afloat. The impact is also evident in the market for locally used vehicles.” The dealer explained that a Nigerian-used 2005 Toyota Corolla, which previously sold for between N750, 000 and N850, 000, now costs between N4.3 million and N4.5 million, further limiting the number of prospective buyers able to afford a car. Identifying the exchange rate as one of the major factors driving the price increases, the dealer said the cost of importing vehicles has risen alongside customs duties and other clearing expenses. He recalled that clearing a Corolla previously cost between N200,000 and N350,000, but now requires between N2.5 million and N3.5 million. While saying that rising cost of clearing imported vehicles has placed additional pressure on dealers and customers, he pleaded with the government to review the situation, warning that the combination of high import costs and weak purchasing power was hurting the business. He also linked the decline in patronage to the rising cost of living, noting that higher rents, food prices and other household expenses had left many Nigerians struggling to meet basic needs. “You wouldn’t expect somebody who is struggling to survive to look at buying a car”. item.title: Spain Begins Three-Day Mourning After Latest Train Tragedy Kills 68
item.description: Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday after its second high-speed rail collision this year killed 68 people and injured scores, with relatives desperately seeking news about their loved ones. One of Europe’s deadliest train disasters this century has raised fresh questions about safety on Spain’s rail network after the transport minister reported an “error” and “inexplicable circumstances” that led to the crash. The collision happened in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha on Wednesday morning when a service by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo. Emergency services combed through the wreckage at night to find further victims on the key line linking Madrid with the southern city of Seville, hoisting pieces of mangled metal with cranes, AFP reporters saw. Josimar Medina, a 31-year-old Peruvian who was holidaying in Spain with his girlfriend, said he was sleeping on the Renfe train when “I woke up and I was in the air.” Pablo Mejia, 42, escaped with injuries to his head, telling AFP that a last-minute change of seat saved his life. Wearing a bloodstained grey jumper and holding his tattered suitcase, he recounted “a very strong hit… a lot of people on the floor, on top of each other, seats ripped out, suitcases, a lot of chaos”. “I think I’ve been born again,” he said. Members of the Parliament observe a minute of silence for the victims of a fatal train crash in Spain at the end of the state budget debate at the Portuguese parliament in Lisbon, on October 28, 2026. ‘Long And Hard Hours’ A school in the nearby village of Urda, around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid, is being used to allow relatives to enquire about their loved ones. Teams of Red Cross workers offered support to groups of people who arrived, some of them in tears, amid crowds of police and journalists from around the world. Red Cross psychologist Carmen Garcia said “long and hard hours” were in store because “every person will manage it in their own way. “We have people who are in shock, who haven’t taken on board what has happened, angry people, sad, worried people. The grieving will be complicated,” Garcia said. People arrive at a support center for relatives of missing victims in Urda, following the train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo, on October 28, 2026. The Civil Guard has set up four offices in the cities of Madrid, Toledo, Cordoba and Seville to enable relatives of the victims to provide DNA samples and help identify the missing. Blood donation points have also been set up in Castilla-La Mancha and Madrid. item.title: Over 50% of financial industry ready for data localisation — CBN
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) yesterday said that more than 50 per cent of Nigeria’s financial industry is ready to comply with data localisation requirements, stressing that the country must strengthen its digital sovereignty without undermining innovation and global technology integration. The Director, Payment System Supervision Department, CBN, Dr. Rakyat Yusuf, disclosed this at the CBN-National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) Executive Regulatory Dialogue on the National Sovereign Cloud Initiative (NSCI) and data localisation in Lagos. Yusuf said a survey conducted by the apex bank showed that more than half of the industry was prepared to comply, expressing optimism that the remaining institutions would make progress following clarifications provided at the dialogue. “A survey we conducted to generate data on the level of preparedness has shown that more than 50 per cent of the industry is ready to comply,” she said. She added: “Ultimately, we expect everyone to be on board by January 2027 to ensure that payment data is properly localised.” According to her, the policy is about “our sovereignty, clarity and visibility over our transaction data,” as well as ensuring financial system stability.” Yusuf said the CBN’s priority was to support financial institutions in achieving compliance rather than resorting immediately to sanctions. “However, where we identify a deliberate attempt to avoid compliance, sanctions will come into play. There will be sanctions for non-compliance,” she warned. Also speaking, the Deputy Governor, Financial System Stability, CBN, Lamido Yuguda, said Nigeria must strengthen control over its critical digital infrastructure while remaining open to global technological developments. He said: “The objective of the National Sovereign Cloud Initiative should not be to constrain innovation or isolate Nigeria from global technological developments. Rather, it should provide the security, resilience, and regulatory certainty necessary to support investment, innovation, and sustainable growth.” Yuguda said the resilience of the financial system increasingly depended on the digital infrastructure supporting it. He added: “We must strengthen digital sovereignty while remaining globally competitive; enhance security without constraining innovation; and promote localisation while ensuring that the financial system continues to benefit from efficient and reliable technology.” Meanwhile, NITDA Director-General, Kashifu Abdullahi, assured financial institutions that Nigeria’s technology ecosystem had the capacity to support the implementation of the sovereign cloud initiative. “Today’s workshop is to give you the assurance that the technology exists, the Nigerian tech ecosystem is capable, and it can support you in complying with your regulator’s mandate or directive,” he said. item.title: Hardship: Our problems with FG’s 90-day relief plan —Labour
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young In an apparent response to growing public concern and outcry over the high cost of living and the worsening economic hardship confronting Nigerians, the Federal Government recently announced a 90-day relief plan aimed at providing succour to workers and the wider population. However, rather than inspire confidence, the initiative has come under intense scrutiny from the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, which questions its transparency, effectiveness and capacity to address the underlying causes of the crisis. The labour centre has described the intervention as a “confession, not a solution,” arguing that temporary palliatives cannot replace concrete measures to tackle rising living costs, declining purchasing power and widespread impoverishment. The NLC also demanded the disclosure of the details of the plan, alongside concrete action on wage awards, petroleum prices, tax relief and the review of the national minimum wage, arguing that Nigerians need practical solutions rather than another set of promises. In this interview with Vanguard, NLC Assistant General Secretary, Chris Onyeka, explains the labour movement’s reservations about the plan, outlines its demands for urgent economic relief and challenges the Federal Government to move beyond promises and implement sustainable solutions to the hardship facing Nigerian workers and the masses. Onyeka said: “Our response to the federal government’s so-called 90-day plan to ease the cost of living is unambiguous. This plan is not a remedy; it is a confession. It is the government’s tacit admission, finally dragged out of it by the sheer weight of popular suffering, that its policies of the past nearly four years have afflicted the Nigerian people rather than improved their lives. “For years, the government denied that its reforms were producing pain. Various Ministers told us there was no suffering while other official spokespeople insisted the economy was on the right track. Now, with the announcement of a 90-day cost-of-living plan, the government has conceded the obvious; something is deeply wrong, and it was caused by the very policies it once defended. “But a confession is not a cure and, a plan cobbled together in panic is not a plan for the people. It is perceptibly playing politics with the genuine cries of Nigerian workers and masses. ‘We haven’t seen the plan’ “The truth is that we have not seen the Plan neither have any citizen It claims to help. We know that the most basic demand of any democratic governance is transparency. Yet nobody; not us in the NLC, not civil society, not the Nigerian workers and masses facing the crisis of survival daily; has seen this 90-day plan or knows what it contains. Any genuine plan to reduce the suffering of Nigerian workers would be a welcome development. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 29, 2026
item.description: Trading in Nigeria’s foreign exchange market opened on Thursday with the local currency displaying steady conditions against the United States dollar across both official and unofficial channels. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the Naira traded around N1,346.05 per US dollar. Spot market activity recorded moderate intra-day movements as commercial banks and corporate entities executed transactions for foreign trade, import bills, and capital remittances. The rate maintains a tight range following ongoing liquidity support and market interventions from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) aimed at easing demand pressure. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, street traders and Bureau De Change operators in major hubs including Lagos, Abuja, and Kano quoted buying rates around N1,375 per dollar, while selling rates floated near N1,385 per dollar. The parallel market premium remains relatively narrow compared to the official rate. Market analysts attribute the market stability to sustained external reserves, which hold above $55 billion. Strong foreign inflows from oil exports and diaspora remittances continue to support liquidity across both FX channels. Market participants expect trading conditions to remain stable as regular commercial order flows are absorbed throughout the business day. item.title: 84.9m informal workers face retirement without safety net
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The National Pension Commission, PenCom, is stepping up efforts to expand pension coverage among Nigeria’s self-employed and informal sector workers, as an estimated 84.9 million people remain without pension coverage, exposing a significant gap in the country’s retirement security system. Figures presented at the 2026 Annual PenCom Media Conference in in Lagos, showed that although the informal sector accounts for an estimated 93 per cent of Nigeria’s workforce, only 242,690 informal sector workers had enrolled in the Personal Pension Plan, PPP, as of July 2026. The figures, based on estimates of the informal sector workforce, put pension coverage among the group at just 0.29 per cent, highlighting the challenge facing efforts to bring millions of traders, artisans, farmers, professionals and gig workers into the pension system. The Personal Pension Plan was introduced under Section 2(3) of the Pension Reform Act, PRA, 2014 to extend pension coverage to self-employed persons and workers in the informal sector who may not have access to conventional employer-sponsored retirement savings arrangements. The scheme allows eligible contributors to make flexible payments daily, weekly, monthly or at their convenience, depending on their income and circumstances. Registration requires a National Identification Number (NIN) and a phone number, while prospective contributors can register directly with a Pension Fund Administrator (PFA) or through an accredited pension agent. However, the presentation identified several obstacles to wider participation, including irregular earnings, limited awareness, distrust of financial institutions, preference for readily accessible savings, geographical barriers and gaps in digital literacy. For many informal sector workers, whose earnings may fluctuate considerably, setting aside money for retirement can be difficult when contributions compete with immediate household and business expenses The presentation also noted that access to a pension account does not necessarily translate into sustained savings, as some contributors may register without making regular or subsequent payments. It stressed that the success of the Personal Pension Plan should therefore be measured not only by the number of registered accounts but also by active contributors, frequency of contributions, consistency of saving, average account balances and the adequacy of retirement benefits. Under the Plan’s contribution structure, 50 per cent of contributions constitutes the contingent portion, which may be withdrawn three months after the initial contribution and subsequently once every two months. item.title: $21.7bn external borrowing plan is investment, not debt – Oyedele
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru The Federal Government has put a strong defence to its proposed $21.7 billion external borrowing plan, describing it as a long-term investment in infrastructure, human capital and economic growth rather than an additional debt burden. The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, made the clarification while briefing State House correspondents at the end of the Federal Executive Council, FEC meeting, presided over by President Bola Tinubu at the Council Chamber, presidential villa, Abuja. He said the five-year project financing plan was designed to create productive assets whose long-term economic value would outweigh the cost of borrowing. Presenting the highlights of the Federal Executive Council (FEC) meeting, Oyedele said the plan covered critical investments in transportation, defence and security, health, agriculture, energy, digital infrastructure, small businesses, social protection, environmental protection and education. He disclosed that about $10.6 billion had been earmarked for transportation infrastructure, including major highway projects such as the Sokoto-Badagry and Lagos-Calabar coastal highways, as well as the Kano-Kaduna Metro Rail project. The minister, however, clarified that the proposal was a financing plan submitted to the National Assembly and did not mean the entire amount had already been borrowed or would necessarily be drawn down in full. According to him, the Federal Government was acting as the coordinating authority for external financing covering federal, state and other public-sector projects. He said approximately $4.8 billion of the proposed financing was allocated to projects involving state governments, the Federal Capital Territory and other subnational entities, agencies and development finance institutions. Oyedele said about $7.9 billion would come from multilateral and bilateral development partners, including $5 billion from the World Bank at concessional rates averaging 2.1 per cent. He added that the indicative average interest rate on the commercial component was 7.8 per cent, which he said was below the rate on Nigeria’s November 2025 Eurobond. The minister argued that borrowing could strengthen the country’s balance sheet if the resulting investments generated assets and economic benefits exceeding their financing costs. Using the Dangote Refinery as an illustration, he said large-scale projects often required external financing to be completed within a reasonable period, adding that Nigeria needed to adopt a similar approach to transformative infrastructure. On the state of the economy, Oyedele said Nigeria’s economic indicators had improved since President Bola Tinubu introduced major reforms in May 2023, although he acknowledged that significant challenges remained. item.title: Pushback over N70,000 allowance
item.description: The leadership of the Trade Union Congress (TUC) on Wednesday rejected the federal government’s proposed six-month N70,000 transportation allowance for workers. The Congress, which described the government’s plan as a “haphazard measure” to cushion the effects of fuel subsidy removal, demanded an immediate salary increment for workers. Daily Trust reports that the government had on Tuesday approved a N70,000 monthly transport allowance for public servants, beginning in November, to cushion the impact of rising living costs. The approval was one of the resolutions reached at a conciliation meeting between the federal government and the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) in Abuja on Tuesday. ADC postpones Sokoto presidential campaign Lagos convenes investors at COP31, advances US$50bn climate investment potential This followed renewed pressure from organised labour over workers’ welfare, the rising cost of living and outstanding agreements. At the meeting, the government also approved the payment of outstanding peculiar allowance arrears, effective from May 1, 2026, in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. The meeting, which lasted several hours, witnessed a lot of disagreements and a series of back-and-forth, according to a senior labour leader who spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity on Wednesday. “What we first demanded during the meeting was immediate reduction of the fuel price, but those on the government side opposed it. This led to disagreements for hours before the chief conciliator appealed to everyone. “After all the back-and-forth, the government side proposed N70,000 transport allowance for six months, not tagged wage award this time, and we reached a consensus on this,” the source said. Although the parties agreed to immediately constitute a Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee, they failed to agree on the effective date for implementing the national minimum wage. A memorandum of understanding signed at the end of the meeting, where the resolutions were contained, showed that leadership of the TUC was not part of the decision. Checks showed that the MoU was signed by the Director-General of Budget, Timi Yakubu; NLC President, Joe Ajaero; the Permanent Secretary, Service Welfare Office, Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Dr Garba Abdul S.U. and the Minister of Labour and Employment, Maigari Dingyadi. TUC kicks The TUC argued that while it is good to negotiate minimum wage, which will affect other cadres of workers, the government must raise the wage level immediately. Speaking to journalists in Abuja shortly after rising from its National Administrative Council (NAC) meeting, the President of TUC, Festus Osifo, who was flanked by the General Secretary, Nuhu Toro, said there are no laws or historical practices stopping the government from doing so. item.title: Alleged $2.1m land deal: Lawyers bicker over case against Wike’s son
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — Two senior lawyers have engaged in a war of words over the ongoing case concerning an alleged $2.1million Abuja land transaction involving Jordan Nyesom-Wike, son of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT. Jordan’s lawyer, Dr. Ogwu Onoja, SAN, accused Ibrahim Waru, counsel to the claimants, of distorting the facts of the case with lies which, he said, were aimed at tarnishing the reputation of his client, who, he said, openly denied any involvement in the alleged land racket during his court appearance. He insisted that his client neither had any transaction with the claimants nor admitted collecting the money. “This haze of lies and malicious fabrication appears to be an orchestrated media campaign intended to whip up sentiments, compromise the mind of the public and intimidate the judge. “For the record, Jordan Wike, in his defence before the court, stated in unequivocal terms that he has never met Safwan Garba G.Y. or any of his agents at any time. “He maintained this line of defence while giving evidence in court on September 28 and 30, 2026. One, therefore, wonders why a lawyer would grant interviews to misrepresent what transpired in court weeks after the proceedings. “It is baffling that this interview by I.G. Waru was granted this week at the Federal High Court, Abuja, close to a month after the proceedings at the FCT High Court. It is clearly the source of defamatory comments, unfounded claims and unproven conclusions being made on social media by ignorant members of the public,” Onoja, SAN, added in a statement he made available to journalists. However, reacting to the statement, yesterday, Waru insisted that his clients were in possession of the signature of Wike’s son on the acknowledgement receipt for the $2.1million paid for the disputed land. Waru said the interview was granted to sensitise members of the public to the honest and true facts of what actually transpired, in light of the distorted facts widely and wrongly circulated on social media. According to him, nothing said in the interview was contemptuous, conclusive, undermining or overreaching. “Despite the claim of Jordan Wike denying ever knowing or meeting Safwan Garba GY, the WhatsApp chats, whose number Jordan Wike admitted to be his, not only confirmed the familiarity between the duo but also established discussion and understanding regarding the giving and taking of the sum of $2.1million, the subject in contention.” He said it was common knowledge that a civil case is distinct from a criminal case and that both can be pursued concurrently. item.title: Alleged plot to shift poll: it’s fake news, we’re unaware — Presidency
item.description: •ADC-PCC insists on allegation plot, warns Tinubu •Reps call for INEC briefing on preparedness By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Luminous Jannamike & Gift ChapiOdekina THE Presidency has described as fake news allegations that the Federal Government was planning to shift the January 16 elections. African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, had earlier raised an alarm over alleged plot to pressure the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, into shifting the January 16 presidential election, warning President Bola Tinubu against seeking to evade an electoral verdict. But Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, while reacting to the allegation, said the government was unaware of any move to shift the election. “The federal government is not planning to shift the date of the election or postpone any election. This is not in the works; the federal government is unaware of this, and this is just fake news as far as we are concerned.” However, the council said it had received information that INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, would be summoned to the Presidential Villa and instructed to alter the election timetable, with just 80 days to the poll. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the council urged Tinubu to abandon any such move and called on Amupitan to reject any instruction to change the date and immediately make any such approach public. “The election date belongs to Nigerians. It must not be rewritten behind closed doors at the Villa,” the council said. It said Nigerians had endured three and a half years of soaring prices, shrinking incomes and relentless hardship, insisting that they must be allowed to judge the Tinubu administration at the ballot box on January 16. “A government that has made life this difficult for Nigerians must not be allowed to postpone its day of judgment,” it said. While acknowledging Ebola as a serious public health concern, the council said health professionals must be allowed to contain the disease, adding that INEC must take necessary steps to protect voters and election workers. It cited the position of the Director-General of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, NCDC, that there was currently no reason to postpone the election, warning against using the health emergency as a political justification for delay. The council also put INEC, domestic observers and international election monitors on notice, demanding that any proposal to alter the timetable be made openly, backed by published health evidence and subjected to public scrutiny. “The Presidency must not use a health emergency to escape an electoral verdict,” it added. At press time, the electoral commission was yet to react to the development. item.title: FG approves East, West super grids to raise transmission capacity to 19,000MW
item.description: •Pays N1.23trn of N3.3trn power sector debt By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA—THE Federal Government said yesterday it has approved the commencement of procurement for the proposed East and West super grids, as part of efforts to strengthen the national electricity network and raise transmission capacity from about 5,000 megawatts to 19,000MW within two years. Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this while briefing State House correspondents at the end of the Federal Executive Council, FEC, meeting presided over by President Bola Tinubu, at the Council Chamber, Presidential Villa, Abuja. He explained that the projects would improve grid resilience and enable the country evacuate more electricity to consumers. “The East and West Super Grids are not projects for one part of the country. They cut across the north and south of Nigeria, strengthening the backbone that must carry power from where it is generated to where it is needed,’’ he said. The initiative is designed to address one of the sector’s central contradictions: Nigeria has more than 13,000MW of available generation capacity, but its transmission network can reliably wheel only about 5,000MW. Tegbe said the super grids would improve resilience, reduce grid instability and allow more electricity to reach homes, businesses and industries. He said: “The target is simple. We want a grid that can evacuate the power we already have, not one that leaves generation stranded while consumers remain in darkness.’’ The minister explained that the corridors would strengthen transmission links from Sokoto through Abuja and other locations into parts of southern Nigeria. Beyond the super grids, the council approved three immediate interventions for Abuja and the Lagos axis, two of the country’s most important electricity demand centres. The first is a 33kV double-circuit underground and overhead line connected to the Katampe Transmission Substation, a major hub serving the North-Central region. The second covers the design, manufacture and supply of three 300MVA, 330/132/33kV transformers for the Ikeja West Transmission Substation, a critical node supplying Lagos. The third will reconstruct and upgrade the 35.6-kilometre Itumola–Mapasin–Shagamu 132kV single-circuit line into a double-circuit line to serve rising demand along the Lagos–Shagamu corridor. “These are not glamorous projects, but they are the projects that determine whether power actually gets to the consumer,” Tegbe said. On sector liquidity, the minister disclosed that the federal government had paid N1.23 trillion of the N3.3 trillion owed gas suppliers and other power-sector stakeholders. “We have paid N1.23 trillion, and we intend to finish the job. But we must also stop new debts from accumulating,’’ he said. The post FG approves East, West super grids to raise transmission capacity to 19,000MW appeared first on Vanguard News .

Senator Barau Jibrin who noted that Osinbajo got it wrong , said the administration of President Bola Tinubu was taking steps to address what he described as longstanding challenges confronting the country. According to Jibrin, while Osinbajo’s concerns, particularly those drawn from Afrobarometer surveys on Nigeria and other African countries were valid, the government needed to improve communication with the people to highlight ongoing efforts to address the challenges. Recall that Osinbajo, who served as Vice-President under former President Muhammadu Buhari from 2015 to 2023, had expressed concern in his lecture about the failure of democratic governance among citizens across Africa after almost three decades of uninterrupted democratic rule in several countries. Citing Afrobarometer surveys, Osinbajo, who was defeated by President Bola Tinubu during APC presidential primary, ahead of the 2023 elections, highlighted widespread dissatisfaction with democratic institutions, economic hardship, declining public confidence in government and diminishing youth participation in electoral politics. He noted that although 64 per cent of Africans preferred democracy to other forms of government, only 38 per cent were satisfied with the way democracy was working in their respective countries. Osinbajo also cited findings indicating that 59 per cent of Africans considered their national economies to be in bad shape, while 51 per cent said their economies had deteriorated. He further expressed concern over the rising cost of living, unemployment, inadequate access to healthcare and declining voter turnout, warning that persistent hardship could weaken public confidence in democracy, particularly among young people. But replying the former vice president at a public lecture, titled ‘’Democracy and Development: Rethinking the Leadership Question,’’ in Yola, Adamawa State, to commemorate the 59th birthday of Governor Ahmadu Fintiri yesterday, Barau described Osinbajo’s lecture as thought-provoking and intellectually stimulating. He,however, said the gloomy picture painted by the surveys was being addressed and that the gaps were partly attributable to inadequate communication between governments and citizens. item.title: Manufacturers raise alarm over N1.35trn alternative power costs, 18,935 job losses
item.description: *Say growth crawls at 1.41%, despite broader economic recovery *Urge FG to cut energy, financing costs lAcknowledge govt’s import-duty, value-added tax relief on 875 pharmaceutical raw materials By Victor Ahiuma-Young & Omotola Aremo LAGOS — Manufacturers under the aegis of Chemical and Non-Metallic Products Employers Federation, CANMPEF, said yesterday they were facing mounting pressure from soaring energy costs, expensive credit, weak consumer demand and job losses, despite improvements in the country’s key macro-economic indicators in 2025. The federation also raised alarm over the worsening cost of doing business, citing an estimated N1.35 trillion spent by local manufacturers on alternative power in 2025, alongside the loss of 18,935 manufacturing jobs in the first half of the year. President of CANMPEF and Vice President of the Dangote Group, Chief Devakumar Edwin, who raised the alarm at the Federation’s 46th Annual General Meeting, AGM, in Lagos, called on the Federal Government to urgently address the high cost of energy and financing, harmonise taxes and levies and strengthen support for local production. He said: “Nigeria’s economy grew by 3.87 per cent in 2025, up from 3.38 per cent in 2024, while headline inflation declined and the foreign exchange market became more stable. However, these improvements have yet to translate into meaningful gains for manufacturers. “Manufacturing grew by only 1.41 per cent in 2025, compared with 1.20 per cent in 2024, while its contribution to real Gross Domestic Product fell to 8.05 per cent from 8.24 per cent.’’ Edwin described the situation as a major concern for the industrial sector, stressing that macro-economic stability must translate into stronger industrial output, job creation and export growth. “Our central message is that this stability must now translate into competitiveness in the form of sustainable jobs, increased output and exports. ‘’Although the economic reforms introduced from mid-2023 had delivered measurable improvements in inflation, foreign exchange stability and economic growth, manufacturers continue to grapple with high operating costs that undermined production and investment. Most of these gains have yet to reach the factory floor,” the CANMPEF president stated. ‘Electricity supply is major constraint’ He identified electricity supply as one of the most significant constraints confronting manufacturers, particularly producers of chemicals, plastics, rubber, glass, ceramics and other non-metallic mineral products, many of which depended on energy-intensive production processes. “Despite installed grid capacity exceeding 13,000 megawatts, average delivered generation remained below 5,000MW, against estimated demand of about 18,345MW. The shortfall, attributed to gas-supply constraints, transmission bottlenecks and recurring grid collapses, has forced many manufacturers to depend on alternative power sources at considerable expense,’’ Edwin said. item.title: What happens after INEC declares a winner?
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye After the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) declares a winner of the presidential election, the Commission must publish the candidates’ scores and the name of the person returned as elected. The winner is then issued a certificate of return, while the election result may still be challenged through the legal process. The declared winner does not begin the presidential term immediately. Under the Constitution, the four-year term begins when the president-elect takes the oaths of allegiance and office. What is a certificate of return? INEC must issue a sealed certificate of return to a candidate returned by the returning officer within 14 days. The certificate formally records that the candidate has been declared elected. INEC must also publish a notice showing the candidates’ scores and who was returned. Can the result be challenged? Yes. A candidate or political party that participated in the election may file an election petition. For a presidential election, the Court of Appeal hears the petition. The Constitution requires an election petition to be filed within 21 days after the result is declared. Separately, the Electoral Act gives INEC power to review a declaration or return within seven days if it receives a report from its officials and is satisfied that the declaration was made under duress or knowingly and wilfully contrary to specified result-verification procedures. When does the winner take office? The winner takes office after being sworn in at the start of the new presidential term. The Constitution provides that a president’s four-year term begins on the date the president takes the oaths of allegiance and office. So, the declaration makes the winner president-elect; the inauguration begins the term. The post What happens after INEC declares a winner? appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Solid Minerals: FG Inaugurates Nigeria-US Committee On Strategic Cooperation
item.description: The Federal Government has inaugurated the Nigeria-United States Committee on Strategic Cooperation in the Solid Minerals Sector in Abuja to advance the partnership with the US. This came weeks after the Federal Government and the United States of America signed a memorandum of understanding to boost the development of Nigeria’s solid minerals sector. The agreement was signed on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly between Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, and the US Deputy Secretary of State, Christopher Landau, at the Nigerian Mission House in New York, United States. The minister, who inaugurated the committee, however, refuted claims that Nigeria sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to America. “I inaugurated the Nigeria-United States Committee on Strategic Cooperation in the Solid Minerals Sector in Abuja to advance our partnership with the United States and set the record straight on reports claiming Nigeria sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to America,” Alake stated in a post on X. “Let me be very clear. Nigeria has not sold its mineral assets.” He explained that the agreement signed with the US was a government-to-government framework designed to connect American investors with Nigerian businesses. “It is about attracting investment, sharing technology, expanding local processing and creating jobs. “Under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s leadership, we are determined to move beyond an economy heavily dependent on oil,” he said. The minister stated that Nigeria’s mineral resources must create greater value at home and deliver lasting benefits to Nigerians. “That is why local processing is now a key requirement for investors seeking mineral titles. “Our partnership with the US offers an opportunity to match Nigeria’s vast resources with the capital and technology needed to build a stronger mining industry. The progress we are seeing in mineral processing reflects this direction,” he added. Alake urged the committee to approach the responsibility with diligence, identify viable investment opportunities and turn the agreement into measurable results that support President Tinubu’s $1 trillion economy target. According to him, the focus is ensuring that Nigeria’s mineral wealth creates jobs, strengthens our economy and delivers real value to our people. At the signing of the MoU in September , the minister had said that the implementation would achieve the economic diversification goals of the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu and boost industrial growth. Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, and the US deputy secretary of state Christopher Landau, at the Nigerian Mission House in New York, United States, during the pact signing. The Deputy Secretary of State Landau was quoted as expressing strong agreement with Nigeria’s position, adding that as Africa’s fastest-growing economy and most populous country, Nigeria is a regional power that deserves partnership with the US.

item.title: Chelsea Win As Bayern, Madrid Share Points In Women’s Champions League
item.description: Goals from Ellie Carpenter and Kadeisha Buchanan were enough to secure a second win for Chelsea in this season’s Women’s Champions League on Wednesday, while Bayern Munich came from two goals down to draw with Real Madrid. Chelsea, who reached the final in 2020-21, opened their campaign with a win and a draw despite scoring just once in their first two games. They looked nailed on for another win in the first half at Plough Lane as they dominated the game without getting a goal. Alyssa Thompson hit the crossbar while Aggie Beever-Jones, put away by a superb pass from Hannah Hampton, was denied by a last-ditch challenge from Shukurat Oladipo. That changed in the 51st minute when Wieke Kaptein cut the ball back for substitute Carpenter, making her 50th Champions League appearance, who slid the ball under the goalkeeper Rachele Baldi. Melvine Malard missed a golden chance to put the game to bed, but Buchanan sealed it a minute from time, heading Kaptein’s cross into the Roma net. Bayern Munich’s Spanish forward Edna Imade (R) celebrates scoring the 1-2 goal with her teammates during the UEFA Women’s Champions League – League phase, Matchday 3 – football match between FC Bayern Munich and Real Madrid in Unterhaching near Munich, southern Germany, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) There was a moment’s silence before kick-off at the Sportpark Unterhaching in Munich as a mark of respect after at least 68 people were killed in a train crash near Madrid earlier on Wednesday. Real Madrid, who were all wearing black armbands, took an early lead when Athenea found the net in the seventh minute. They doubled their lead 15 minutes later when former Bayern forward Lineth Beerensteyn headed home from close range, her first goal for Madrid in the Champions League since her move in the summer. Real Madrid’s Spanish forward Athenea del Castillo (C) celebrates scoring the opening goal with her teammates during the UEFA Women’s Champions League – League phase, Matchday 3 – football match between FC Bayern Munich and Real Madrid in Unterhaching near Munich, southern Germany, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) / ALTERNATIVE CROP Bayern hit back shortly after when Edna Imade met Klara Buhl’s corner from the left and powered her header into the net. And they drew level in the 52nd minute when Momoko Tanikawa curled in from the edge of the box after Madrid keeper Merle Frohms parried out a shot from Linda Dallmann. Swiss side Servette dispatched Belgium’s OH Leuven 5-1 with Paola Hernandez and Gloria Marinelli scoring two goals each. Wednesday’s late matches see Arsenal host Benfica while eight-time winners Lyon are at home to Inter Milan. item.title: Tinubu To Present 2027 Budget Before End Of 2026
item.description: President Bola Tinubu is expected to present the 2027 Appropriation Bill to the National Assembly before the end of 2026. The Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning, Doris Uzoka-Anite, disclosed this on Wednesday when she briefed State House Correspondents on some of the outcomes of the Federal Executive Council Meeting chaired by President Bola Tinubu at the Council Chamber of the State House. She also said that the FEC had officially endorsed the National Development Plan 2026–2030 alongside new legal frameworks designed to tackle child stunting and boost national food security. Speaking with correspondents following the council meeting, Uzoka-Anite announced the key approvals while reflecting on the successful conclusion of the 32nd edition of the Nigerian Economic Summit (NES) held in Abuja from October 26 to October 28. Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr. Doris Uzoka-Anite. She said FEC also approved a Revised National Policy on Food and Nutrition (2026) to replace older frameworks to establish sustainable financing and strengthen inter-ministerial collaboration across agriculture, livestock, health, education, and development partners. Earlier, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, clarified that the $21.7 billion borrowing proposal transmitted to the National Assembly by President Bola Tinubu is an investment in assets and not for spending. Oyedele explained that the proposed $21.7 billion plan represented a multi-year investment plan spanning roughly five years rather than an immediate drawdown. He disclosed that $10.6 billion of the money was slated for critical transport links, including the Sokoto–Badagry Highway, Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, and the Kano–Kaduna Metro Rail. Oyedele said that over $7.9 billion of the loan would be sourced from multilateral and bilateral development partners (led by $5 billion from the World Bank) at an average interest rate of just ~2.1 per cent. He said $3.3 billion is earmarked directly for state government projects, with an additional $1.45 billion set aside for the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), ​out of the overall package.
